note: Product-intent confirmation record, built to the two-field rule the 2026-11-17 brief sets out: the INTENDED product (ASIN, official listing URL, confirmation date, source) and the OBSERVED redirect target are two different questions and are stored in two different objects that are never merged. The intended-product fields are empty on every row, because no value has been supplied or confirmed for them: the brief gives a link, not an ASIN, and each supplied token is 9 characters where Amazon's own definition of an ASIN is 'the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products' (BD-12, read live 2026-11-17). A filled-in intended-ASIN field here would be an inference, so it is left blank and the row is marked UNVERIFIED. The observation fields are full: each supplied URL does resolve, reproducibly, to one live listing, and that is a fact about the link's behaviour, not about the product's identity.

intent.rule: These four travel together and describe ONE thing: the product the submitter meant, confirmed against an official listing. They are empty or they are all four filled. There is no partial state.

observation.rule: These describe what the supplied URL did when fetched. They never populate an intent field, and an intent field never borrows a value from them.

asin_definition.text: ASIN is the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products.
